name: Mia
situation: Mia, 19, plays netball. She limped in this morning, holding her right ankle.
diagnosis: Grade II lateral ankle sprain (anterior talofibular ligament)
story: Yesterday Mia went up for a rebound, landed on an opponent's foot and rolled her right ankle into inversion and plantarflexion. She felt a pop on the outside, and it swelled within the hour. She hobbled off the court and could weight bear. She sprained the same ankle two years ago and never did any rehab. Finals are in four weeks. The ATFL is torn partially (grade II), the CFL is intact, there's no fracture (Ottawa rules negative), and her balance on that side is poor, which puts her at risk of chronic instability.

findings.hpc: Went up for a rebound yesterday, landed on someone's foot and rolled the ankle inwards. Felt a pop on the outside.
findings.body_chart: Pain on the outside of the right ankle, just in front of and below the lateral malleolus.
findings.pain_behaviour: Worse walking and on stairs. Ice and elevation help.
findings.pain_24h: Throbs at night if the foot hangs down. Stiff first thing.
findings.previous_episodes: Rolled the same ankle two years ago. No rehab, it just settled.
findings.goals: Wants to play the finals in four weeks.
findings.swelling: Moderate swelling around the lateral malleolus with early bruising. The figure-of-eight is 2 cm larger than the left.
findings.gait: Antalgic gait, shortened stance on the right, avoids push-off.
findings.observation: Swollen lateral right ankle, bruising tracking toward the heel.
findings.ottawa_ankle: No bony tenderness at the posterior edge or tip of either malleolus, the navicular or the base of the 5th metatarsal. She took four steps on arrival. Ottawa rules negative.
findings.palpation: Exquisitely tender just anterior and inferior to the lateral malleolus, over the ATFL.
findings.rom_ankle: Plantarflexion and inversion are painful and limited. Dorsiflexion is a little stiff (knee to wall 6 cm vs 11 cm). Eversion is fine.
findings.ankle_drawer: Increased anterior translation compared with the left, soft end feel, pain over the ATFL.
findings.talar_tilt: Mild pain with a firm end feel. The CFL seems intact.
findings.syndesmosis: Squeeze and external rotation tests negative.
findings.standing_balance: Single leg stance on the right lasts 8 s with eyes open. The left lasts more than 30 s.
findings.y_balance: Anterior reach on the right is 7 cm shorter than the left.
findings.hop_squat: Unable to hop on the right because of pain.
findings.imaging: None ordered. Not indicated with negative Ottawa rules.
findings.mmt: Eversion strength 4/5 and painful. Everything else 5/5.

name: Daniel
situation: Daniel, 42, is a storeman. His GP has sent him in with back pain that's now going down his right leg.
diagnosis: Right S1 radiculopathy from an L5/S1 disc herniation
story: Three weeks ago Daniel bent and twisted lifting boxes at the warehouse and felt his back go. A few days later the pain started travelling down the back of his right thigh and calf to the outside of his foot, with pins and needles in the little toes. Now the leg hurts more than the back. Sitting, driving, coughing and sneezing make it worse. A posterolateral L5/S1 disc herniation is irritating the right S1 nerve root: positive SLR and slump, reduced ankle jerk, weak calf, reduced sensation on the lateral foot. There are no cauda equina signs. He's scared he's done something permanent and is avoiding bending altogether.

findings.hpc: Lifting boxes three weeks ago, bent and twisted, felt his low back go. Leg pain started a few days later.
findings.body_chart: Right low back, then the back of the thigh and calf to the lateral border of the foot. The leg is worse than the back.
findings.neuro_symptoms: Pins and needles along the outside of the right foot and the little toes.
findings.pain_behaviour: Worse with sitting, driving, coughing and sneezing. Eased by walking and side lying.
findings.pain_24h: Can settle at night lying on his side. Morning stiffness lasts about 15 minutes.
findings.cauda_equina: No saddle anaesthesia, and bladder, bowel and sexual function are normal. Symptoms in the right leg only.
findings.red_flags: No weight loss, cancer history, fever or trauma.
findings.beliefs: Scared he's done permanent damage. Avoiding bending at all.
findings.social: Storeman on light duties. Married with two kids.
findings.observation: Slight lateral shift away from the right.
findings.rom_lumbar: Flexion to mid-shin reproduces right leg pain. Extension causes local back pain only.
findings.slr: Right SLR reproduces calf and foot pain at 40°, worse with added dorsiflexion. Left is 80° and pain-free.
findings.slump: Positive on the right. Symptoms ease with neck extension.
findings.reflexes: Right ankle jerk reduced. Knee jerks equal.
findings.myotomes: Right plantarflexion weaker. L4 and L5 myotomes strong.
findings.calf_raise: Right single leg calf raise: 8 reps. Left: 20.
findings.dermatomes: Reduced light touch over the lateral border and sole of the right foot.
findings.paivm: Central PA at L5 reproduces back pain only.
findings.imaging: None yet. Not indicated without red flags.

name: Margaret
situation: Margaret, 68, came into hospital on Monday. The nurses say her left leg gives way when she tries to stand.
diagnosis: Right middle cerebral artery ischaemic stroke with left hemiparesis
story: On Monday Margaret was making a cup of tea when her left arm suddenly went heavy and useless. Her husband Bill called an ambulance. A CT showed a right middle cerebral artery infarct, and she was thrombolysed. Five days on she has a left hemiparesis: weak quadriceps that let the knee buckle in standing, low tone in the arm, an inferiorly subluxed left shoulder, reduced sensation and proprioception, an up-going left plantar response and left-sided inattention. She has high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes. She lives with Bill in a two-storey house and was fully independent before. She wants to go home and get back to her garden.

findings.hpc: Making a cup of tea on Monday when her left arm suddenly went heavy. Her husband called an ambulance.
findings.medical_notes: Thrombolysed on admission. Medically cleared to mobilise. Systolic BP target under 180.
findings.obs: BP 146/84, HR 78 regular, SpO2 96% on room air.
findings.imaging: CT and CT perfusion: right middle cerebral artery territory infarct.
findings.meds: Aspirin and atorvastatin started this week. Metformin.
findings.social: Lives with her husband in a two-storey house, five steps to the front door with one rail.
findings.prior_function: Fully independent. Walked daily, gardened and drove.
findings.goals: Go home and get back into the garden.
findings.falls_history: No falls. Not allowed up on her own.
findings.observation: Sitting slumped to the right in bed, left arm resting in her lap, head turned to the right.
findings.mmt: Left hip flexion 3/5, knee extension 2/5, dorsiflexion 2/5, shoulder flexion 1/5. Right side 5/5.
findings.myotomes: Left side globally weak. Right side normal.
findings.tone: Low tone in the left arm. Normal to slightly reduced in the left leg.
findings.reflexes: Left biceps and knee jerks brisker than the right.
findings.umn: Left plantar response up-going. Right down-going.
findings.dermatomes: Light touch reduced across the whole left arm and leg, not in a dermatomal pattern.
findings.proprioception: Impaired joint position sense at the left big toe and fingers.
findings.neglect: Misses targets on the left on a cancellation test and doesn't turn to the left spontaneously.
findings.cranial_nerves: Mild left lower facial droop. Forehead sparing.
findings.cognition: Alert and orientated. Speech is clear.
findings.coordination: Can't test on the left because of weakness. Normal on the right.
findings.subluxation: One finger-breadth inferior subluxation at the left shoulder.
findings.sitting_balance: Sits unsupported on the edge of the bed, weight shifted right, and corrects when cued.
findings.sit_to_stand: Assist of 2. Weight stays through the right leg, and the left knee buckles into flexion when she shifts left.
findings.bed_mobility: Rolls to the right independently. Needs assistance to roll left.
findings.mas: Motor Assessment Scale: sit to stand 2, walking 0.
findings.berg: Not safe to complete yet. Standing is limited by left knee instability.

safety.message: Stood Margaret up before checking medical clearance and vital signs.

name: Robert
situation: Robert, 71, is on the surgical ward, day one after abdominal surgery. His oxygen needs are creeping up.
story: Robert had an open right hemicolectomy through a midline laparotomy yesterday for bowel cancer. He smoked for 40 years and quit five years ago. The wound hurts so much that he barely presses his PCA, breathes shallow and fast, and won't cough properly. He hasn't been out of bed. His lung bases have collapsed (bibasal atelectasis): reduced breath sounds and dullness at the bases, reduced basal expansion, a rising oxygen requirement and a low-grade temperature, with some secretions he can't clear. Before surgery he walked the dog for 30 minutes every morning.

findings.medical_notes: Open right hemicolectomy via midline laparotomy yesterday for a bowel tumour. No complications in theatre.
findings.obs: RR 24, SpO2 91% on 2 L nasal prongs (it was 96% on room air yesterday), HR 98, BP 118/70, temp 37.6.
findings.imaging: Chest x-ray: plate-like atelectasis at both bases, worse on the right. No consolidation or effusion.
findings.abg: On 2 L: PaO2 62, PaCO2 38, pH 7.42. Mild hypoxaemia.
findings.bloods: Hb 112, WCC 11.2, CRP 84, as expected the day after surgery.
findings.pain_score: 7/10 on moving and coughing. Rarely presses the PCA because he dislikes the feeling.
findings.pain_behaviour: Any deep breath or cough catches at the wound.
findings.breathlessness: Can't take a full breath. Not distressed at rest.
findings.cough_sputum: Feels something rattling but can't get it up.
findings.prior_function: Independent. Walks the dog for 30 minutes every morning.
findings.social: Lives with his wife in a single-level home.
findings.observation: Lying slumped low in the bed with IV, PCA, catheter, abdominal drain and nasal prongs.
findings.breathing_pattern: Shallow, rapid, apical breathing. No accessory muscle use.
findings.auscultation: Reduced breath sounds at both bases, right worse than left, with fine late inspiratory crackles. Coarse sounds centrally.
findings.chest_expansion: Reduced basal expansion on both sides.
findings.cough_test: Weak, moist cough. He holds his abdomen and can't clear the secretions.
findings.bed_mobility: Needs help of 1 to roll, splinting the wound.
findings.dvt: Calves soft and non-tender. On enoxaparin.

safety.message: Mobilised Robert before checking his vital signs.

name: Gary
situation: Gary, 58, is a plumber. His left shoulder has been aching for two weeks.
diagnosis: Cardiac ischaemia (angina or acute coronary syndrome) referring to the shoulder. Call 000.
story: For two weeks Gary has had a heavy ache in his left shoulder that spreads down the inside of his arm and once into his jaw. It comes on climbing stairs or carrying tools up a ladder, goes away after five minutes of rest, and doesn't come on with overhead work. It brings sweating, breathlessness and once nausea. He smokes a pack a day, stopped his blood pressure and cholesterol tablets, and his father died of a heart attack at 60. The shoulder exam is completely normal. It came on again walking in from the car park today. This is cardiac ischaemia, and he needs 000, not treatment.

findings.hpc: No injury. A heavy ache started in the left shoulder two weeks ago.
findings.body_chart: Deep ache in the left shoulder, sometimes down the inner arm. Once into the jaw.
findings.pain_behaviour: Comes on climbing stairs or carrying tools up a ladder and goes after five minutes of rest. Overhead reaching doesn't bring it on.
findings.pain_score: 4/10 when it comes on. A bit there right now, after walking in from the car park.
findings.pain_24h: Never wakes him. Only comes with exertion.
findings.associated: Gets sweaty and puffed when it comes on. Felt sick once.
findings.breathlessness: Gets puffed on stairs, more than he used to.
findings.cardiac_risk: Smokes a pack a day. High BP and cholesterol, stopped his tablets. Father died of a heart attack at 60.
findings.smoking: A pack a day for 35 years.
findings.pmhx: Told he had high blood pressure and cholesterol. Stopped the tablets last year.
findings.meds: None. Stopped his antihypertensive and statin.
findings.red_flags: No weight loss or fever. Symptoms are exertional and come with sweating.
findings.social: Self-employed plumber, under houses and on roofs.
findings.obs: BP 168/98, HR 96, SpO2 96%. Looks a little clammy.
findings.observation: Slightly pale and clammy. Rubbing his chest.
findings.rom_shoulder: Full active range in all directions, pain-free, no painful arc.
findings.prom_shoulder: Full and pain-free with normal end feels.
findings.rom_cervical: Full and pain-free. Doesn't reproduce the arm symptoms.
findings.ecg: No ECG available in the clinic.
findings.exercise_tolerance: Don't. Exertional testing with these symptoms is unsafe.

safety.message: Ran an exertional test on Gary while he had active cardiac symptoms.
